programme: NR1H2 (LXRβ) carries the macrophage/hepatic cholesterol-handling programme: its targets ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE, SCARB1, CETP, LPL, PLTP and SREBF1 are the core reverse-cholesterol-transport and HDL-remodeling circuit that LXR nuclear receptors run. AEBP1 sits on the uptake side of the same lipid axis, acting on APOE, CD36 and FABP4 — the scavenger-receptor/fatty-acid-binding machinery that drives macrophage lipid loading. Together the two describe the lipid-laden, cholesterol-handling macrophage state that builds and remodels atherosclerotic plaque.
role_in_a: In cardiovascular disease this programme is the mechanistic core of atherosclerotic plaque formation: LXR-driven cholesterol efflux (NR1H2 target genes) versus scavenger-receptor lipid uptake (AEBP1 target genes) sets the balance between foam-cell formation and plaque regression in the vessel wall.
role_in_b: In stroke, the same macrophage cholesterol-handling balance operating in carotid and cerebral vasculature is a recognized driver of large-artery atherosclerotic plaque, the mechanism behind a substantial share of ischemic strokes; NR1H2's Open Targets stroke percentile (0.19) is modest but present, consistent with a contributing rather than a headline role.
shared_axis: Atherosclerosis is the vascular lesion that cardiovascular disease and ischemic stroke are both built on; a macrophage lipid-handling programme (LXR efflux genes opposed by scavenger-receptor uptake genes) operating in coronary/peripheral versus cerebral vessels would produce disease in both territories through the same cell-level mechanism, explaining why the two disease labels co-occur in this network.
reasoning: The module is nameable from the targets alone (classic LXR reverse-cholesterol-transport genes plus classic foam-cell uptake genes), and NR1H2's own record places it in cardiovascular-adjacent settings, but nothing retrieved ties NR1H2 or AEBP1 to stroke or cardiovascular disease by name — the disease link runs through the well-established general fact that atherosclerosis underlies both, not through a documented pair-specific source. NR1H2's support (16/24) is well above AEBP1's (12/24), so the LXR/efflux side of the story is better anchored than the uptake side.
support: PMID 33788111 — studies LXRβ (NR1H2) expression in epicardial/subcutaneous adipose tissue of patients undergoing evaluation for coronary disease, placing the factor in a cardiovascular-adjacent lipid context; PMID 27021877 — shows NR1H2 modulating macrophage-driven aneurysm formation in a vascular-disease mouse model, again cardiovascular-adjacent rather than naming stroke. No retrieved paper places AEBP1's CD36/FABP4/APOE axis in either named disease directly.
how_to_falsify: In monocyte-derived macrophages from matched cardiovascular-disease and stroke cohorts, measure whether NR1H2 occupancy/expression tracks ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE and SCARB1 induction concordantly across the two disease groups, and whether AEBP1 levels track CD36/FABP4 induction the same way; if cholesterol-efflux gene induction and foam-cell uptake-gene induction do not co-vary with NR1H2/AEBP1 activity across the patient groups that generated the network, the proposed module is not what is driving the observed concordance.
caveats: Networks were built from blood, a proxy tissue for the macrophage/vessel-wall biology the programme actually runs in, so the signal here is indirect. Only 24 patient-group comparisons drawn from 4 independent cohort pairs support this pair, a modest base for either factor. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed canonical vascular/endothelial and inflammatory regulators (KLF2, TAL1, ERG, CEBPB, STAT1, IRF1) — their absence reflects that filter, not a gap in the lipid story. The single-view list includes several interferon-pathway factors (IRF5, IRF6, IRF9) that might have suggested an antiviral/inflammatory account instead; they did not recur and are correctly excluded here.
